rv.q: Head on down to see International City Theatre's fabulous summer entry and you’ll see exactly what I mean.

This is the stuff of high tragedy, and International City Theatre’s production of DiPietro’s four-hander powerfully dramatizes history while also making the personal political, with touches of humor in a highly entertaining retelling of true-life events worthy of the ancient Greek bards.
What gives the play its searing relevance is how little translation some of those ideas require today.

The result is a production that comes close to delivering a powerful examination of conscience, courage and political independence but leaves the audience wishing it had trusted Margaret Chase Smith’s story more.

cn.t: Critics praise Joe DiPietro's timely look at Senator Margaret Chase Smith's stand against McCarthy, finding it a fascinating and relevant examination of political courage that resonates powerfully with today's divisive climate.
